newsitem.title: NORWAY: Aker settles Sleipner dispute, pays 340 mln cowns.
newsitem.headline: Aker settles Sleipner dispute, pays 340 mln cowns.

text.p: Norwegian construction and offshore group Aker ASA said on Thursday it had settled a dispute with the Insurance Group of the Sleipner A platform.

Under the settlement all claims made by the Insurance Group in connection with the loss of the Sleipner platform have been withdrawn in exchange for the payment of 340 million Norwegian crowns ($52.37 million) as of January 31, 1997.
Aker said the payment did not represent an admission of any liability for the loss.
Aker subsidiary Norwegian Contractors (NC) was building Sleipner's concrete gravity base for state oil company Statoil when it sank in a fjord near Stavanger in August 1991.
NC delivered a replacement gravity base in 1993, two years after the sinking, and Aker paid penalties of 130 million crowns for the delay.
But Aker and the platform insurers have until now been unable to agree a settlement and in March 1995 the insurers sued Aker for 2.3 billion crowns.

"Aker/NC have entered into the settlement agreement on the basis of a total evaluation where consideration of Aker's freedom of action, and the uncertainty that has been created for the group have been important factors," a statement said.

Aker said it and NC had also entered a 45 million crown settlement agreement with the Sleipner Group with respect to a 211 million crown claim put forward by the group for defect provisions in the Sleipner contract.
"This implies that all issues regarding possible claims in connection with the Sleipner incident have now been solved," Aker said.

It said the settlements would have limited impact on Aker and NC profits. NC has accruals of about 300 million crowns. The agreement would have a negative impact on Aker's 1996 net profit of about 60 million crowns, the company said. ($1=6.492 Norwegian Crown)
